findings.title: The step-failure row now offers a select step's argv as a recovery that cannot attach the change
findings.recommendation: Scope the recovery and its 'unattached until that recovery lands' consequence to publish and tail steps. For a failed select step, the select row governs: the line names the failure and that the change proceeds unattached for this invocation, and shows no recovery (running the switch would not attach the change, because publish is never called). Edit the row once and re-sync the checked mirror; a text assertion in pr-references.test.ts can hold it.
findings.reproduction: Read rows 126 and 127 of the delta together for a select whose `create` step (git switch -c <branch> --no-track <remote>/<default>) fails. Row 126 says publish is never called and generation proceeds unattached. Row 127, as the walk rewrote it, shows the failed step's argv as 'the recovery the user runs' and says the change 'proceeds unattached until that recovery lands' — but running that switch after generation attaches nothing, since no publish follows. Before the walk (67dffea6:spec.md:127) a single-step select failure had no skipped step, so no recovery was shown.

commentary: Graded each resolved entry over its sweep scope against the walk commit 91222cdc and ran the residual check from b485c7c2 (the external return's commit). Eight edits are present, complete and clean: the two archive-reference notes read record fields that tail actually prints (observations.pr_state, reason.detail.recovery.case); the unstaged filter is exercised by a test that fails when the filter is reverted; the retarget note now matches validatePrUrl's observed/expected; the arc-done readout's outcome list matches program.ts's finish calls one for one. The one regression is a cross-row interaction: widening the step-failure row to show the failed step is right for publish and tail, but the select row ends the PR layer, so for select the shown argv is not a recovery of anything. Passes 0 and 6 not run (verification genre).
